value.title: Docker build infra + base daemon framework
value.summary: Engine-agnostic build+run container pair, compose stack with pgvector, throwaway /health daemon, and paved docker verbs.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: "Stand up the docker substrate for fs3: a BUILD container (pinned rust toolchain, persistent cargo caches in named volumes) and a RUN container (slim, binary mapped in) so a source change reaches the running daemon without any image rebuild and without restarting Postgres. Extend s001's db-only docker-compose.yml with a daemon service, prove the loop with a throwaway /health daemon, and pave the whole surface as a docker harness extension (verbs may shell through to script files) so agents never improvise engine commands. Engine-agnostic throughout: OrbStack today, podman by construction - compose-spec only, engine binary configurable. The build container is designed for later CI reuse (cross-platform matrix) but CI is not wired here."

sections.name: goals
value: Fast dev loop: source change -> new binary running in the daemon container with zero image rebuilds; only the daemon service restarts, Postgres stays up.
Build+run container pair: builds happen INSIDE a build container (pinned toolchain, cargo registry+target caches on named volumes); the run container maps the binary in.
Engine-agnostic: works on OrbStack now and podman by construction - compose-spec-valid file, configurable engine binary, no Docker-exclusive features.
Linux binaries from the mac host via the build container (native arm64, no emulation).
Paved docker surface: a harness extension with stack up/down/status, build, daemon restart, logs, exec, and one-shot run-in-build-container - implementation may shell through to script files.
Compose stack complete from day one: pgvector Postgres (already landed by s001) plus the daemon service this plan adds.

sections.name: non_goals
value: Real daemon functionality: the /health daemon is a throwaway POC - no config loading, no endpoints beyond /health; a later plan replaces it with the real fs3-daemon service surface.
CI wiring: the build container is designed for CI cross-platform reuse (pinned toolchain, no host assumptions) but no CI pipeline is created here.
PG schema/store design - deferred to the store plan; this plan only proves the pgvector container serves the extension.
Zero-restart binary swap: a plain per-service container restart is the accepted reload (Jordan 2026-08-26).
Host-side cross-compilation (cargo zigbuild): rejected in favour of building inside the build container (Jordan 2026-08-26).
Live podman verification: podman compatibility is by construction (compose-spec + engine var); live verification waits until a podman host exists (open question).

value.claim: From a clean checkout on a machine with a compose-capable engine, the paved stack-up brings up daemon + Postgres and `curl http://127.0.0.1:<port>/health` returns 200 from the containerized daemon.

A source change reaches the running daemon container with ZERO image rebuilds: the paved build runs in the build container reusing persistent cargo caches, and only the daemon service restarts - the db container's StartedAt is unchanged across reloads.
The Postgres service serves pgvector: `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector` succeeds, and data survives daemon reloads and stack down/up via the named volume.

The build container produces a Linux (aarch64) binary from the mac host with the toolchain pinned in the image - `file` reports an ELF executable; incremental rebuild after a 1-line change avoids dependency recompiles.

A docker harness extension paves stack up/down/status, build, daemon restart, logs, exec, and one-shot run-in-build-container; each verb is documented, discoverable via the harness surface, and green on the installed engine.

Engine-agnostic by construction: the compose file validates against the compose spec, every script honours a configurable engine binary (docker/podman), and a lint proves no Docker-exclusive features are used.

value.title: Phase 1: POC - build/run containers, compose stack, /health daemon (plan assets only)
value.brief: Prove every mechanism in docs/plans/002-docker-daemon-base/assets/poc/docker/ with zero collision with the in-flight s001 stream: build container with cached incremental builds, throwaway /health daemon, POC compose (db + daemon), reload loop that never touches the db container, engine-agnostic lint, results writeup.

value.title: Phase 2: Integrate - extend root compose, wire fs3-daemon, pave the harness extension
value.brief: GATED: starts only after s001's phase exit (fence overlap on docker-compose.yml and .harness/extensions/). Promote the proven POC shapes: extend the s001 db-only docker-compose.yml with the daemon service, add docker/ (Dockerfiles + scripts), wire the real fs3-daemon binary, land the docker harness extension + docs, and prove in-container test runs.

sections.name: research_context
sections.value: "No research-dossier; grounded instead in: s001's landed substrate (7-crate workspace b812d4d; db-only docker-compose.yml with pgvector/pgvector:pg16, host port 5433, named volume, healthcheck - its header explicitly defers the daemon service to this plan), workshop 001 architecture rules (still binding: daemon deps live in fs3-daemon), and PRD reqs 15-20 (daemon), 33 (compose stack), 4 (central PG+pgvector)."

value.rationale: Infrastructure plan - every task's proof is a runnable command against real containers; no unit-test surface worth mocking.
value.focus_areas: stack boot, health reachability, cache-warm incremental build timing, db-uptime-across-reload, pgvector extension, engine-var honouring
value.excluded: podman live runs (no podman host), CI, load/perf beyond build timings

value.location: Hybrid: README.md quick-start pointer + docs/how/docker.md guide (phase 2)
value.rationale: Repo convention from plan 001; the harness extension's discoverable verbs are the primary agent-facing docs.

sections.name: risks_assumptions
sections.value: "Assumes an OrbStack (or docker-compatible) engine on dev machines; assumes s001 lands its phase exit before phase 2 begins; assumes arm64 linux containers are acceptable for the dev loop (x86_64 is a CI-matrix concern); pgvector image pinned at pgvector/pgvector:pg16 per s001."

value.question: When to live-verify podman compatibility (needs a podman host or CI runner) - until then podman support is by construction only.
value.note: Jordan's call; lint + compose-spec validation stand in meanwhile.

value.why: Feasibility questions (cache-warm incremental speed in-container, volume-mapped binary reload, engine-agnostic compose) are answerable only by running code.
value.key_questions: Covered by Phase 1 POC tasks - timings, reload behaviour, engine lint; results land in assets/poc/docker-results.md.

value.question: Dev-loop shape: host cross-compile + mount, or build inside a container?
value.answer: Build container + run container pair; builds happen inside the build container (Jordan: 'we just build inside a build Docker container... a build container and a run container').

value.question: Engine support?
value.answer: OrbStack now, podman must work - 'we use orbstack not docker... we should support podman etc too so careful of super docker native stuff'. Engine-agnostic by construction.

value.question: Reload on new binary?
value.answer: Per-service container restart is fine ('Yeah, we can restart the container, that's fine'); db must NOT restart on binary updates.

value.question: Daemon scope for this plan?
value.answer: Throwaway POC: 'a HTTP endpoint that is a health check. We will replace this soon anyway, so just make it as basic as possible'.

value.question: Include Postgres now?
value.answer: Yes - 'include the PG vector stuff now... setting up a Docker Compose from the start'; s001 already landed the db-only compose, phase 2 extends it.

value.question: Harness extension verb set?
value.answer: stack up/down/status, build, daemon restart, logs, exec + 'there should be stuff to run things in there as well' (one-shot run in the build container). May 'just call through to just file commands' (scripts).

value.question: CI relationship?
value.answer: 'later we can use the build container in CI as well to do our cross-platform stuff' - design for reuse, do not wire CI.

value.question: Workflow mode / testing / docs?
value.answer: Simple ('this plan can be very simple thanks'); testing lightweight proof-by-running; docs hybrid README + docs/how (repo conventions inherited).

value.effect: phase 2 EXTENDS the compose file; daemon binary comes from fs3-daemon

value.notes: Workshop 001 respected: no new crates/ports; daemon-side deps stay in fs3-daemon; POC daemon is throwaway and lives in plan assets.

sections.name: implementation_summary
sections.value: "Two phases. Phase 1 (runs NOW, parallel to s001): prove everything as a POC under the plan's assets - build container with named-volume cargo caches, throwaway /health daemon, POC compose, reload loop, engine lint, results writeup. Phase 2 (GATED on s001 phase exit + o-prime fence coordination): extend the root docker-compose.yml with the daemon service, add docker/ Dockerfiles + scripts, wire the real fs3-daemon binary, land the docker harness extension (verbs shell through to the scripts) + docs/how/docker.md, and prove in-container test runs."

value.finding: s001 already landed a db-only docker-compose.yml (pgvector:pg16, port 5433, named volume, healthcheck) whose header defers the daemon service to a later plan.
value.action: Phase 2 EXTENDS this file - never replaces it; db service definition stays untouched.

value.finding: Cargo caches (registry + target) must live on NAMED VOLUMES, not mac bind mounts - VirtioFS/osxfs overhead destroys incremental build times; source bind-mount read-only is fine.
value.action: tk-0101 mounts source ro + two named cache volumes; timing proof in done_when.

value.finding: Apple Silicon engines (OrbStack, podman machine) run arm64 linux natively - the dev loop needs no emulation; x86_64 output is a CI-matrix concern for later.
value.action: Dev loop targets aarch64-unknown-linux; build container designed to take a --target matrix later.

value.finding: podman compatibility means compose-spec discipline: no docker-exclusive features (e.g. develop/watch, docker-specific extensions); engine binary must be configurable.
value.action: All scripts honour FS3_ENGINE (default docker); tk-0105 lints for violations; compose validated with `compose config`.

value.finding: Jordan ruled the harness extension may shell through to plain script files - the harness verb is the discoverable surface, scripts are the implementation.
value.action: docker/scripts/* are the single implementation; the extension and humans call the same scripts.

value.mitigation: Phase 1 is fully independent (plan assets only); phase 2 waits on the o-prime gate.

value.risk: In-container incremental builds still too slow despite cache volumes

Phase 2 gated on s001 exit; o-prime coordinates the fence.

sections.name: execution_guardrails
value: Engine-agnostic always: every script honours FS3_ENGINE (default docker); no Docker-exclusive compose features; compose-spec-valid file.
Never rebuild an image for a source change; never restart the db service in the reload loop.
POC daemon is throwaway: /health only, no config, no gold-plating; phase 2 wires the real fs3-daemon binary.
Phase 1 writes ONLY under docs/plans/002-docker-daemon-base/assets/poc/**; root compose, docker/, and .harness/extensions/** are phase-2 paths gated on s001 phase exit.
Workshop 001 (plan 001) architecture rules still bind: exactly two ports, no new crates, daemon-side deps in fs3-daemon only.
Never hand-edit any .dd.md (ddocs is the writer) or the-flow files (CLI-only).

Shared volumes between build script and compose use explicit fixed names (`name:`/`external: true`) - compose project-name prefixing otherwise silently splits them; the paved down never deletes cache volumes.
